summary: L-4 pyramid-roof lookout in Mendocino National Forest; build year 1932 or 1934 by source; condemned 1990, restored 1993; staffed May to October in 2026.

facts.design: L-4 pyramid roof design; wooden 14 by 14 foot live-in cab with catwalk on a 10 foot wood tower

events.note: Register gives 1932; a local history gives 1934 (see resolved_conflicts)
Forest Lookouts page says the CCC constructed it in 1934; a 1994 Ukiah Daily Journal item says the California Conservation Corps built it
A July 19, 1940 item names Ralph McCombs as having charge of the lookout station
Tower enclosed for year-long staffing as an enemy aircraft warning station during World War II
May 29, 1946 item: a lookout established on Anthony Peak with a Covelo man in charge
June 21, 1956 item: manned for fire detection; equipment packed in the last mile past a snowdrift
Found unsafe and condemned after continuous use until then

Rehabilitated to its original configuration by the Forest Service and volunteers (Forest Lookouts); the Register credits the Forest Service and the Twin Rocks Landowners Association with the restoration
July 1994: Covelo Ranger District announced a dedication ceremony to reopen the lookout
North Pass Fire (about 42,000 acres, much of it on the Covelo Ranger District); building wrapped in foil for protection (September 4, 2012 item)
Article says staffed each year from May to October

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register gives 1932. Forest Lookouts gives 1934 and quotes a 1994 Ukiah Daily Journal item saying the California Conservation Corps built it in 1934. Not resolved; the story gives both.

corrections.proposed: remove (no total height in sources read)
corrections.why: Register describes a 10 foot wood tower under a 14 by 14 foot cab; no source read gives a total height of 8.8 m (about 29 ft). Left out of facts.

notes_for_editor: Two substantive sources agree on the 1993 restoration, 1994 registration and the 1990 condemnation; they disagree on build year (1932 vs 1934). The 2026 staffing claim comes from a single article (kymkemp.com) that appears to repost a Forest Service item; treat as seasonal staffing as reported. Sources read do not say whether the public may visit or climb the tower; rental status not found. The Register visit report from 2007 records staffed yes but was not cited. Elevation in a peakbagging entry (6,960 ft) differs from the Register's 6,891 ft; the Register figure is used. Height 8.8 m in our record is unsupported; see corrections. No photos added.
